entities.name: Anemia of chronic inflammation
observations: Low serum iron with low TIBC and elevated ferritin indicates inflammation-mediated iron sequestration and impaired iron delivery to erythroid marrow.
Ferritin can rise as an acute-phase reactant and does not necessarily indicate readily usable iron.

entities.name: Occult gastrointestinal bleeding
observations: In a 63-year-old man, occult gastrointestinal blood loss remains clinically important, but isolated absolute iron deficiency usually causes low ferritin and high TIBC.
Inflammation can mask coexisting iron deficiency by elevating ferritin.

entities.name: Inflammatory iron restriction
observations: Hemoglobin 8.9 g/dL, MCV 70 fL, ferritin 400 ng/mL, iron 50 micrograms/dL, and TIBC 200 micrograms/dL yield transferrin saturation about 25% and most strongly support anemia of chronic inflammation among the answer choices.
